[donman92] Keen to use as a portable air jerky maker. Using a cooling rack. This will be far more efficient.
[ezekiel181] These seem awesome at first until you realise the manufacturing shortcuts taken to get to this price.
We bought one at $45 because we dry in the living room and it folds up really compact but holds a lot.
Initially it was amazing.
Holds plenty, folds up to a smallish cylinder that fits beside a desk or counter. So good we went and bought another one 2 days later.
After a few weeks we noticed problems with both.
The arms and legs share a space so after some wear and movement things don't align perfectly anymore. Sometimes the arms won't go inside because of the legs or you fold the legs and drop the body only for the arms to shoot out the top.
They should have had guides for each rod or separate chambers.
Then if you collapse the arms by dropping them inside instead of carefully lowering them down the white caps on the arm tips fly off and the arm disappears inside the body! Now the legs don't go back properly and neither do half the arms.
Those caps are kept on by little metal pins shot through under the tip many of which are loose from the start.
I would have gladly paid an extra $2 for 16 screws.
Finally the arms are prevented from popping right out of the body by small protrusions pushed from the inside of the aluminium tube out to make studs. These are woefully inadequate. The arms are also held horizontal by the tiniest margin of plastic at the rear of the arm.
Together this means either you lift the arm up and it pops right out. Or as you're placing clothes plastic edge lets go and your shirts on the floor
We have to hold the arm when sliding dry clothes off.
Designed and printed a bunch of parts to try to fix them with limited success.
Eventually threw out the worst one and kept the other. It bothers me every single night we hang clothes.
I went to the Kmart website to leave a review and found you have to order online and be invited to review anything.
So here's my review and I hope every search for this POS product finds this.
Edit: also a light breeze knocks it over if fully loaded.
[donman92] This is why I prefer to use it as an air jerky dryer; you want a direct fan in a corner where it can't move much.
